summary: Age of Innovation is a standalone reimplementation of Terra Mystica, where players guide one of twelve asymmetric factions terraforming hexes into their preferred terrain type to build and upgrade structures, forming a growing network of connected buildings. It's a dense, spatial-puzzle euro where proximity to opponents both constrains your expansion and grants bonus resources, making the shared map the central strategic battleground.
praised: deep asymmetric faction design with genuine strategic variety
tight economic engine with meaningful upgrade paths
strong replayability from faction and map combinations
criticised: steep learning curve and heavy rules overhead
long playtime, especially at higher player counts
can feel very tight/unforgiving if you fall behind the terraforming curve
fiddly bookkeeping with many tracks and resources to manage

interaction.kind: area proximity and indirect competition for terrain
interaction.detail: Players mostly build out their own faction's network on their own terrain colors, but the shared hex map means adjacency to opponents' buildings grants power/resource bonuses and contested terrain can block expansion, so the map itself is the main shared state rather than direct conflict.

scoring.why: Victory points accumulate from round-by-round action scoring, cult track final scoring, network/area bonuses, favor and bonus tiles, and building upgrades, none of which reduces to a single dominant source.
scoring.how_you_win: You win by scoring the most victory points overall, earned through building and upgrading structures, advancing on cult tracks, and completing bonus/favor tile objectives across the game.
